mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility means fewer commuting and out-of-home work trips, which removes routine weekday retail footfall and drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -20.1 at t-3w to -24.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below their t-3w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT crossing below -25.0 percent change from baseline signals a sharp reduction in station use that immediately cuts non-essential retail and recreation trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below -25.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than its t-0w value after TRANSIT stays below -25.0.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above 1.0 while TRANSIT is below -22.0, households are staying home and avoiding transit-based trips, which suppresses retail-and-recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 1.3 and TRANSIT was -26.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 1.0 and TRANSIT stays below -22.0.

mechanism_narrative: Weak WORKPLACES combined with falling PARKS indicates that both workday and leisure outdoor trips are contracting, removing two independent sources of retail footfall and driving RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -27.1 and PARKS fell to 1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES stays below -25.0 and PARKS stays below 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, WORKPLACES decline is a policy-driven signal that non-essential activity is being curtailed; RETAIL_REC therefore falls over the next four weeks as restrictions bind.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -21.7 to -27.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES remains below -25.0 under tightening restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: A PARKS reading below 2.0 indicates the outdoor-season peak has passed; reduced park visits lower adjacent retail-and-recreation traffic, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 12.4 at t-2w to 1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean while PARKS stays below 2.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM turning negative to -2.7 shows necessity shopping is contracting faster than discretionary retail; the release of grocery-trip time and the already deeply negative RETAIL_REC baseline favor a mean-reversion rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned negative at -2.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to its last 14-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays below 0.0.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below -26.0, policy restrictions are strongly binding on commuting and transit use; this jointly suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -26.3 and WORKPLACES was -27.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next week is higher than at t-0w while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -26.0.
